clue.text: Hopping mad — we get VAT on traditional British fare

indicators.note: hopping mad describes fury, but hopping also suggests letters jumping about into a new order

explanation.surface: An angry diner rages that VAT is now being charged on a plain old British dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hopping mad' reads as one idiom for furious; 'Hopping' alone is the anagram signal, and MADWEGETVATON rearranges into the four words.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat and two veg is the stock phrase for a plain, traditional British dinner plate.

clue.text: Admit money originally cut

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so the first letter of money

parts.note: its first letter is taken
to own up is to admit, so own means admit

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that the money was cut at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass that has been mown has been cut, the past participle of mow.

clue.text: Dangerous to leave hotel, which is spacious

indicators.note: to leave says the hotel letter departs from the word for dangerous

parts.note: hairy is informal for dangerous or frightening
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A warning that it is unsafe to check out of a roomy hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: An airy room is light and open, with plenty of space and air.

clue.text: One fashionable piece of writing? Could be yes and no

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one
tony is informal for stylish or fashionable
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A stylish essay, perhaps one that weighs yes against no.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by example: yes and no is a pair of opposites.
explanation.definitionFit: Words of opposite meaning are antonyms, and yes and no are a classic opposing pair.

clue.text: Countryman's pronounced stoop

indicators.note: pronounced says the word for the countryman is said aloud

parts.note: a Dane is a man from Denmark, a countryman of that country

explanation.surface: A rural man has a marked hunch in his back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Countryman' suggests a rustic, but here it is a man of a country, a Dane; 'stoop' is the verb, not a bent posture.
explanation.definitionFit: To stoop to something is to condescend to do it, which is what deign means.

clue.text: See 1
Nag's sounding off — wife cross

definitions.note: a noun phrase: the horse's act of crying out

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife in genealogies
a hinny is a cross between a male horse and a female donkey

explanation.surface: Someone is complaining loudly, and his wife is angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' looks like a complainer and 'cross' like angry; the nag is a horse and the cross is a hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A whinny is the high neighing call a horse makes, and a nag is an old horse.

clue.text: Cutting through corruption, start to speak to meeting in a deeply emotional way

indicators.note: cutting through says the letter goes into the middle of the word for corruption

parts.note: vice is depravity or corruption

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: its first letter is taken
a rally is a mass meeting

explanation.surface: A campaigner breaks through the sleaze to address a gathering with real passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something felt viscerally is felt in the gut, instinctively and intensely rather than by reason.

clue.text: Sentimental slush — see right through the German beauty queen?

parts.note: goo is mawkish sentimentality

indicators.note: right through says the word for see sits wholly inside the German article

parts.note: der is German for the
look means see

explanation.surface: A cynic dismisses a pageant as sugary slush, and spots the German winner.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a beauty queen is one kind of good-looker.
explanation.definitionFit: An attractive person is a good-looker, and a beauty queen is a pageant winner chosen for looks.

clue.text: Now their work became less acceptable

indicators.note: work as a verb means knead or shape, so these letters are reworked into new words

explanation.surface: A critic says their output has now fallen out of favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' looks like the noun in their work; it is a verb telling you to rework NOWTHEIR.
explanation.definitionFit: An excuse or joke that wore thin lost its effect through overuse and stopped being tolerated.

clue.text: One type of racing at venue for another — largely a shambles

parts.note: F1, Formula One motor racing, written with I for one

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: Ascot is an English racecourse, a venue for horse racing

explanation.surface: Holding one kind of race at a course built for another is mostly a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: Formula One is written F1, and the 1 becomes the letter I; Ascot is a famous horse-racing course in Berkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is a complete and humiliating failure, a total mess.

clue.text: Poet taking sweetheart round Spanish city

indicators.note: taking says the poet holds the heart letter inside him

parts.note: Ovid was the Roman poet
the heart, or middle letter, of sweet
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A poet escorts his darling on a tour of a city in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' looks like a lover but is the central letter of sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Oviedo is the capital of Asturias in northern Spain.

clue.text: Slightly backtracking, show deference to biblical couple going steady

parts.note: Onan and Eve, two figures from Genesis, written together

indicators.note: only a slight step back: the opening letter of the word for showing deference moves back one place

parts.note: to kneel is to show respect or deference

explanation.surface: A pious courting pair from scripture are taking things steadily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'biblical couple' looks like Adam and Eve but is two names, ONAN and EVE. 'Slightly backtracking' moves the K of KNEEL back one place, making NKEEL.
explanation.definitionFit: On an even keel means stable and balanced, like a ship upright in the water.

clue.text: Protestant archbishop's first proscription overturned — past it sadly

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of archbishop is used

parts.note: its first letter is taken

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition or proscription

indicators.note: sadly means unfortunately, so these letters are put into a different, worse order

explanation.surface: A church leader rejects the old prohibition, now sadly outdated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns BAN into NAB; 'sadly' rearranges PASTIT into APTIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Anabaptists were a radical Reformation movement practising adult baptism, so one is a kind of Protestant.

clue.text: Can you connect with this form of humour?

definitions.text: Can you connect with this form of humour?

parts.words: Can you connect with this form of humour?
parts.note: can is slang for a toilet, so humour you connect with the can is toilet humour

explanation.walkthrough: 'Can you connect with' reads as asking if you relate to it; in British and American slang the can is the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavatorial humour is jokes about toilets and bodily functions, crude bathroom comedy.

clue.text: Escapes, just about, on hearing wife's in the vicinity

parts.note: near means close by, in the vicinity

indicators.note: on hearing says the word for wife is said aloud

parts.note: missus is informal for wife; the clue's possessive points to the plural-sounding form

explanation.surface: Someone overhears that his wife is nearby and only just gets away.
explanation.walkthrough: Missus is British slang for a wife, as in 'the missus'.
explanation.definitionFit: Near misses are escapes from disaster by a narrow margin, close calls.

clue.text: Half, nearly three quarters of words explosive

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: semi- is a prefix meaning half

indicators.note: three of the four letters of the word are kept, the last one dropped

parts.note: a text is a body of words

explanation.surface: Fractions of a speech are said to be explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: Semtex is a plastic explosive made in the Czech Republic.

clue.text: Bill's old trouble

parts.note: an ad, or advertisement, is a bill posted up

explanation.surface: Bill has had old troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; here it is a poster.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado is fuss and bother, as in much ado about nothing.

clue.text: United lifted in first leg a long time ago

indicators.note: lifted in says the word for united is raised and set down inside the other word

parts.note: a stage is a leg of a journey or race, such as the first one
being as one is being united

explanation.surface: A football side, Manchester United perhaps, wins the trophy after the first leg, ages back.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stone Age is the prehistoric era of stone tools, so used loosely for the distant past.

clue.text: Neckwear could be junk, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: a junk is a Chinese sailing boat

explanation.surface: A cast-off scarf may be rubbish, by and large.
explanation.walkthrough: 'junk' reads as rubbish; it is the Chinese ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A boa is a long feather or fur scarf worn around the neck.

clue.text: Plant ground more millet

indicators.note: ground means milled, so the grain's letters are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: A farmer grinds an extra batch of millet.
explanation.definitionFit: An immortelle is an everlasting flower that keeps its colour when dried.

clue.text: Move French regularly interrupting at the back

indicators.note: interrupting says the picked letters break into the word for at the back

parts.note: aft means at the rear, in sailing terms

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken

parts.note: the odd letters of French

explanation.surface: A French intervention at the rear moves things along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move' looks like a physical shift but means stir the feelings; aft is a sailing term for the stern.
explanation.definitionFit: To affect someone is to move or touch them emotionally.

clue.text: Checking work from one of the Royals playing game?

parts.note: a pro is one who plays a game professionally
the Royals is the nickname of Reading FC, the English football club
confirms the pro is a sportsman playing the game

explanation.surface: A member of the royal family takes up a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Royals' looks like the monarchy; it is the nickname of Reading Football Club, and a pro is a professional playing the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Proofreading is reading text to find and correct errors before it is published.

clue.text: Tenor Domingo's initial break

parts.note: first letter of Domingo
a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: The tenor Plácido Domingo gets his first big break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tenor' with Domingo looks like a singer; it means the gist of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The drift of an argument is its general meaning or tenor.

clue.text: Given up before, this smoker

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: ante is Latin for before

explanation.surface: A smoker who quit a while ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given up' reads as quitting smoking; only 'up' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano in Sicily, always smoking.

clue.text: Holed in one side, catamaran partly capsized

indicators.note: capsized says the hidden letters are read backwards
partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A boat overturns after its side is holed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holed' suggests a damaged hull; it is golf.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, a player who aced a hole sank the ball with a single stroke.

clue.text: They may be in bed — one's about to get up

indicators.note: about says the first letters surround the word for getting up

parts.note: I is one, and 's is the letter S, giving IS
to rise is to get up

explanation.surface: Someone is about to get out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' suggests sleep, but it is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Irises are flowers often grown in garden beds.

clue.text: Like a teacher, used role-play at one college

parts.note: did act, performed a role
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tutor tried role-play at a college.
explanation.definitionFit: Didactic means intended to instruct, in the manner of a teacher.

clue.text: 'That OK then?' Lad rudely: 'I'm not interested!'

indicators.note: rudely means roughly, so the letters are put in a crude new order

explanation.surface: A lad brushes off someone checking whether things are all right.
explanation.definitionFit: Talk to the hand is a dismissive retort, meaning the speaker refuses to listen.

clue.text: See 28
